title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Profit is an opinion; cash flow after maintenance and growth capex is the only truth a cyclical manufacturer can spend.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.title: The 10-Year Arc: From FY18–FY21 Contraction to FY22–Q2 FY27 Scale

web_blocks.html: To separate genuine earnings power from accounting noise, you must read SSWL across a full decade [1][18]. Between FY18 and FY21, SSWL hit a revenue ceiling near ₹2,041 Cr (FY19). Sales then dropped 23% to ₹1,563 Cr in FY20 during the auto recession before recovering to ₹1,749 Cr in FY21 [1][18]. Since FY22, the top line has more than tripled. Consolidated sales rose from ₹3,560 Cr in FY22 to ₹4,041 Cr (FY23), ₹4,357 Cr (FY24), ₹4,429 Cr (FY25), and ₹5,183 Cr (FY26), reaching ₹6,235 Cr TTM through September 2026 [1].

web_blocks.takeaway: During the FY19–FY20 downturn, SSWL's revenue dropped 23% while debt stayed sticky near ₹1,000 Cr—demonstrating operating and financial leverage risk when fixed assets are underutilized.

web_blocks.title: Margin Bridge & Separating Core Earnings from the FY24 AMW Write-Back

web_blocks.html: Look closely at the consolidated Profit & Loss table below, especially the March 2024 column [1]. Reported Net Profit in FY24 jumped to ₹675 Cr (EPS ₹42.99), only to drop back to ₹195 Cr in FY25 and ₹190 Cr in FY26 [1]. An automated screener might misread that as an earnings collapse. In reality, FY24 included ₹487 Cr of Other Income (specifically ~₹473 Cr–₹478 Cr in Q4 FY24) representing a non-cash accounting write-back of legacy creditor liabilities following the NCLT acquisition of AMW Autocomponent [1][15]. Strip out that one-time credit, and SSWL's core operating profit marched steadily upward: ₹453 Cr (FY22), ₹443 Cr (FY23), ₹464 Cr (FY24), ₹484 Cr (FY25), ₹510 Cr (FY26), and ₹676 Cr TTM [1]. Operating margin compressed from 13% in FY22 to 10% in FY26 as new Bhuj and knuckle capacity absorbed initial depreciation and start-up costs, before snapping back to 12% in Q2 FY27 on ₹1,930 Cr of quarterly revenue [1][7].

web_blocks.caption: SSWL: Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (FY22–FY26 & TTM)
web_blocks.takeaway: Core Operating Profit grew steadily from ₹453 Cr (FY22) to ₹510 Cr (FY26) and ₹676 Cr TTM; FY24's ₹675 Cr Net Profit was inflated by the ₹487 Cr AMW NCLT liability write-back.

web_blocks.html: Over the past five years, SSWL's Balance Sheet expanded in lockstep with its plant footprint [1]. Fixed Assets plus Capital Work-in-Progress (CWIP) rose from ₹1,457 Cr in March 2022 to ₹2,156 Cr by September 2026 [1]. Meanwhile, Reserves more than doubled from ₹936 Cr to ₹1,969 Cr on retained earnings (Book Value ₹126 per share), with Equity Capital completely unchanged at ₹16 Cr—meaning zero equity dilution over the cycle [1]. Borrowings peaked at ₹1,048 Cr in March 2024 around the AMW transaction, dropped to ₹828 Cr in FY25 and FY26, and rose to ₹914 Cr in September 2026 to support working capital on ₹1,930 Cr of quarterly sales [1]. Note India Ratings' important forensic adjustment: when letter-of-credit (LC) acceptances are included, net adjusted leverage remained above 2.5x EBITDA through FY24–FY26 [4].

web_blocks.takeaway: Reserves more than doubled from ₹936 Cr to ₹1,969 Cr with zero share dilution (Equity Capital flat at ₹16 Cr), while Gross Borrowings stood at ₹914 Cr as of September 2026.

web_blocks.title: Cash Flow Conversion, Working Capital & ROCE Reality Check

web_blocks.html: Does SSWL convert accounting profit into real cash? Across FY22–FY26, cumulative Operating Cash Flow totaled ₹1,796 Cr against ₹734 Cr of Free Cash Flow [1]. FCF was positive in four of five years, turning negative (-₹188 Cr) only in FY24 during the AMW deal [1]. CFO-to-EBITDA conversion averaged 87% across those five years (100% FY22, 89% FY23, 55% FY24, 120% FY25, 73% FY26) [1]. Yet Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) stepped down from 21% in FY23 to 15% in FY25–FY26 (14.8% latest; ROE 11.0%) [1]. Heavy capex—plus ₹138.15 Cr for AMW and Gujarat lines—sits on the capital base ahead of maturity [1][4][12]. That 14.8% pre-tax ROCE confirms SSWL is a capital-intensive cyclical business.

web_blocks.caption: SSWL: Consolidated Cash Flow Statement (FY22–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: SSWL generated positive Free Cash Flow in four of the last five fiscal years (₹143 Cr in FY26, ₹326 Cr in FY25), demonstrating genuine cash conversion despite continuous plant capex.

web_blocks.caption: SSWL: Working Capital Cycle & Return Ratios (FY22–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: Supplier credit (108 Days Payable) offsets elevated Inventory Days (102) to keep Cash Conversion Cycle at 38 days, while ROCE moderated from 21% (FY23) to 15% (FY26) amid heavy capex.

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: The 14.8% ROCE Truth
paragraphs: When you strip away the FY24 AMW accounting write-back and look at five-year cash flows, SSWL passes the earnings-quality test: cash from operations is real, equity dilution is zero, and promoter pledges are gone.

Yet the 14.8% ROCE and 11.0% ROE remind you of the business's physical gravity. Making wheels requires massive presses, furnaces, and inventories. If the ₹1,400 Cr Maharashtra expansion pushes utilization and margins above Q2 FY27's 12.2% OPM, ROCE can climb back toward 18%–20%; if utilization lags, capital intensity will cap returns.

book_paragraphs: To separate genuine industrial cash generation from accounting optics, you have to read SSWL's financials across a full ten-year cycle. Between FY18 and FY21, revenue peaked at ₹2,041 Cr in FY19 before dropping 23% to ₹1,563 Cr in FY20 during India's auto downturn and rebounding to ₹1,749 Cr in FY21. Since FY22, the business has scaled dramatically: sales rose from ₹3,560 Cr in FY22 to ₹5,183 Cr in FY26 and ₹6,235 Cr on a trailing twelve-month basis through September 2026.

One critical forensic adjustment sits inside FY24. Reported Net Profit spiked to ₹675 Cr in FY24 before settling at ₹195 Cr in FY25 and ₹190 Cr in FY26. That FY24 spike was not core earnings; it came from ₹487 Cr of Other Income driven by a one-time non-cash write-back of legacy creditor liabilities after the AMW Autocomponent NCLT acquisition. Stripping out that write-back, core Operating Profit marched steadily upward from ₹453 Cr in FY22 to ₹510 Cr in FY26 and ₹676 Cr TTM, while Q2 FY27 operating margins snapped back to 12.2%.

book_subsections.title: Balance Sheet, Leverage, and Cash Conversion
paragraphs: On the balance sheet, Reserves more than doubled from ₹936 Cr in March 2022 to ₹1,969 Cr in September 2026 with zero equity dilution—share capital remained flat at ₹16 Cr. Fixed assets plus capital work-in-progress climbed from ₹1,457 Cr to ₹2,156 Cr over the same span. Borrowings declined from ₹1,048 Cr in March 2024 to ₹828 Cr in FY25 and FY26 before ticking up to ₹914 Cr in September 2026 to fund record quarterly volumes. India Ratings notes that including letter-of-credit acceptances, net adjusted leverage stayed above 2.5x EBITDA through FY24–FY26.

Cash conversion is solid for a heavy manufacturer: SSWL generated positive Free Cash Flow in four of the last five fiscal years (₹143 Cr in FY26, ₹326 Cr in FY25), averaging 87% CFO-to-EBITDA conversion. However, Return on Capital Employed moderated from 21% in FY23 to 15% in FY25 and FY26 (14.8% latest, with ROE at 11.0%) because continuous capex sits on the balance sheet ahead of full plant maturity. Whether SSWL's next ₹1,400 Cr Maharashtra capex cycle lifts ROCE back toward 18%–20% or compresses it further depends entirely on plant utilization and alloy mix.

Putting all ten years of financial forensics together, SSWL earns a clear fundamental classification: it is a cyclical conditional industrial business with improving operational quality, not a capital-light compounder. It passes the forensic tests that matter most—zero equity dilution over five years, zero promoter pledges, 87% average CFO-to-EBITDA conversion, and four out of five years of positive free cash flow. Yet its 14.8% pre-tax ROCE, 11.0% ROE, >2.5x net adjusted leverage including acceptances, and sensitivity to commercial-vehicle and capex cycles mean that business quality alone cannot justify paying any multiple. That price-blind conclusion sets the stage for the valuation and market-expectation audit ahead.
